newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean daily trumpets defector letter scoop.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean daily trumpets defector letter scoop.

text.p: A South Korean newspaper on Thursday printed a letter attacking Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il that it said was written by a top North Korean official reported by Seoul to be seeking political asylum.
The handwritten letter splashed across the front page of the Chosun Ilbo daily expresses a crisis of faith in a communist system that has produced famine.
If genuine, it would offer an insight into what may have prompted Hwang Jang-yop to betray Pyongyang's "Great Leader" Kim and become the most senior North Korean official ever to defect to the South.
North Korea says Hwang, a close adviser to Kim and one of the architects of Pyongyang's "Juche" philosophy of fanatic self-reliance, must have been kidnapped by Southern authorities.
"The 'ever-so-great general' has come to believe that he is really a genius after all the idolatry showered on him praising him as a great genius," said the letter, referring to Kim Jong-il.
"He has created a dictatorship where his word must be followed. How can a society where people, workers, farmers, and intellectuals starve to death be a socialist society?" wrote Hwang.
"In a feudalistic society the farmers would have staged an uprising by now, but the dictatorship is too tight and too cruel that it would be difficult to expect them to escape such a regime."
The Chosun Ilbo said the letter was delivered to an unnamed South Korean businessman on January 2 by Hwang's aide, Kim Dok-hong, who is also reported to be seeking asylum.
It did not say when it received the note scribbled over four pages.
South Korean officials were treating the letter with caution.
"We have launched a joint investigation on the letter with the foreign ministry and the unification ministry," said a spokesman for the Agency for National Security Planning, the domestic spy agency.
"But we can't confirm at the moment whether the letter exists or was written by Hwang."
The Chosun Ilbo is one of South Korea's leading dailies and often gets scoops on North Korea.
South Korea has released no official details of its dealings with Hwang, but analysts said his apparent defection indicates cracks in North Korea's Stalinist hierachy.
